title: Version 2 document stamps itself Version 1
source: 10 Policy, controls and compliance/Recovery Workbench Personal Data Protection Design v2.docx
description: The file is named v2 and its text is dated 28 October 2026, but the metadata table says Version 1. The source carries no version 2 stamp, so the version it describes is ambiguous.
evidence: v2 metadata table: | Version | 1 | and | Date | 28 October 2026 |; file name Recovery Workbench Personal Data Protection Design v2.docx.
legacy_ref: none (document family, not a legacy story)
proposed: Treat the file name as the version of record; issue this next version as v3 with the source version named in the metadata table.

title: No service owner for any personal data category or control
source: 10 Policy, controls and compliance/Recovery Workbench Personal Data Protection Design v2.docx
description: The design names roles, tables and paths (contact_point.consent_status, PII Kafka, the partner portal) but never names the service that owns the data or the control in the target architecture.
evidence: v2 sections 3, 4, 5 and 8 name tables and roles only; Architecture v5 slide 41 and Ownership Map v1 give the owners, so the mapping is a realignment addition, not a source value.
proposed: Assign every owner from Ownership Map v1 and Architecture v5 slide 41; add the per-service boundary table (section 11) and the enforcement table (section 11.2).

title: Consent state table and column name in the target schema
source: 10 Policy, controls and compliance/Recovery Workbench Personal Data Protection Design v2.docx
description: Consent state is cited as contact_point.consent_status, a monolith table name. The target table is contact_point_ext in rwb_source_data (Ownership Map v1), but the column name is not stated in any source, so the citation cannot be resolved to a column.
evidence: v2 section 3 first bullet: (contact_point.consent_status); Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet: contact_point_ext owner P1, schema rwb_source_data.
proposed: Read the consent state as a column of rwb_source_data.contact_point_ext and carry the exact column name to the P1 DB and API stories when the P1 design fixes it.

title: Version 2 records no approval or document status
source: 10 Policy, controls and compliance/Recovery Workbench Personal Data Protection Design v2.docx
description: The metadata table has no status and no approval, so the document is issued in Draft under the D-RCV-60 overlay.
evidence: v2 metadata rows are Document, Version, Date, Prepared by and Structure only.
proposed: Issue v3 as Draft and leave the approval to the programme governance step after the run.

title: Debt sale tape masking check has no owner and no field list
source: 10 Policy, controls and compliance/Recovery Workbench Personal Data Protection Design v2.docx
section: 4. Minimization and masking; 8. Sharing outside the bank
description: The design requires a masking check on a debt sale tape to the sale terms, but states neither which service selects the fields nor which service performs the check. The per-sale field list is not in the sources.
evidence: v2 section 4 fourth bullet and section 8 second row; Architecture v5 slide 19 gives rwb-debtsale the lots and data room and rwb-integration the buyer file (INT-25); Ownership Map v1 gives debt_sale_lot and debt_sale_account to S6.
proposed: S6 rwb-debtsale selects the fields to the sale terms and P2 rwb-integration performs the check at delivery; the per-sale field list comes from the sale terms, not from this design.

title: PII read log has no event contract
source: 10 Policy, controls and compliance/Recovery Workbench Personal Data Protection Design v2.docx
description: Every read of a personal field is logged through PII Kafka, but the log event's schema, topic and producer contract are not defined in the sources. The path is the ACE Common PII logging to the SOC, not a business topic.
evidence: v2 section 5 second bullet; Architecture v5 slides 8 and 34 (audit and PII logging through ACE Common, separate from business topics); no AsyncAPI event for a PII read in the event catalogue on slides 42 and 43.
proposed: Keep the ACE Common PII Kafka path as the only read log; the field-level event contract is delivered by the ACE team and is not created by any Recovery service.

title: Data subject access retrieval across 19 services
source: 10 Policy, controls and compliance/Recovery Workbench Personal Data Protection Design v2.docx
description: Compliance retrieves the case data within 30 days, but in the target architecture the data is spread over 19 schemas with no single read contract for a rights request. The sources define no retrieval flow for this purpose.
evidence: v2 section 7 Access row; Architecture v5 slides 14 to 20 (one schema and one login per service, no cross-schema reads); Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet.
proposed: Retrieve through each owning service's contract under the Compliance role and scope, with rwb-case (P3) supplying the case ID and case view; no new service is added.

title: Tokenization point and token format are not stated
source: 10 Policy, controls and compliance/Recovery Workbench Personal Data Protection Design v2.docx
description: National ID and passport numbers are tokenized at load, but the sources do not state which component mints the token, whether the token is reversible, or its format. The load is rwb-source-data (P1), which is the only service that reads the ACE views.
evidence: v2 section 4 first bullet; Architecture v5 slides 7 and 15 (rwb-source-data reads recovery.v_ace_* only); Ownership Map v1 gives the extension tables to P1.
proposed: P1 mints the token at load and stores no clear value; the token format and any detokenization path are fixed in the P1 design and the access profile of P4.
